ko.text: The regulator approves the joint app
The app launches with all Must items

name: Merger of Two Companies
tagline: A bank bought a fintech – now they must build one app together
scope: A joint mobile app after a bank acquires a fintech: connection to the core banking system, single sign-on, customer migration, new features and regulatory approval.
intro: A big bank bought a small fintech with a great mobile app. The board wants one joint app for customers of both companies within six months. The bank has a policy for everything, the fintech has a chat for everything. You lead the joint project – with people from both companies.
predWorld: Connection to the core banking system, security audit, AML checks and regulatory approval. Bank policies apply here – and for good reason.
agileWorld: The mobile app, onboarding and new customer features. That's the fintech's strength: try fast, measure and improve.

terms.launch: the launch of the joint app
terms.predShort: core integration, security and regulatory approval
terms.agileShort: the mobile app and new features

stakeholders.name: Bank CIO
stakeholders.quit: blocked deployment to the bank's infrastructure.
stakeholders.epilogBad: put the app into the “standard process” – new versions now ship once a quarter.

stakeholders.name: Fintech founder
stakeholders.wants: speed and his own product ideas
stakeholders.quit: left, taking half of his team along.
stakeholders.epilogBad: left to found a new startup and took the best people with him.

stakeholders.name: Customers of both companies
stakeholders.wants: an app that works and takes nothing away from them
stakeholders.quit: started leaving for competitors in droves.
stakeholders.epilogBad: rate the app two stars and are leaving for competitors.

workstreams.name: Connection to the core banking system
workstreams.why: The bank's core changes once a quarter under strict rules. The interface is designed, approved and built to plan.

workstreams.name: Security audit and AML
workstreams.why: Requirements come from regulation and the audit procedure is prescribed.

workstreams.name: Regulatory approval
workstreams.why: The regulator has deadlines and a list of documents. The filing date is planned.

workstreams.name: Mobile app and onboarding
workstreams.why: What suits customers of both companies only shows in their behavior – you iterate.

workstreams.name: New customer features
workstreams.why: Ideas must be tested with customers before they're built.

workstreams.name: Unifying the design of both brands
workstreams.why: The design is tuned to user reactions, version by version.

workstreams.name: Payroll and accounting of the merged company
workstreams.why: Routine work of the finance department. After the staff transfer it's done by the line organization, not the app project.

workstreams.name: Customer support for existing customers
workstreams.why: Support runs every day and will keep running after the project. It's operations.

backlog.name: Single sign-on for customers of both companies
Connecting the app to the core banking system
Moving bank customers into the app
Handover to bank operations: runbooks and training
Crypto in the app (the founder's idea)
Moving fintech staff into the payroll system

milestones.name: Security audit
milestones.okText: Single sign-on passed the bank's security audit.
milestones.lateText: There was nothing to run the security audit on.

milestones.name: Core integration test
milestones.okText: The app talks to the core banking system and AML checks work.

milestones.name: Regulatory approval
milestones.lateText: The application to the regulator went out late.

milestones.name: Joint app launch
milestones.okText: The joint app is out. Customers of both companies log in with the same button.
milestones.lateText: The app shipped without key features – missing:

shift.title: The founders are leaving
shift.text: The fintech founders sold the rest of their shares to the bank and are leaving. Kuba goes with them and other fintech people are wavering – they feel the bank steamrolled them. Revealed factor: changing people's established habits.
shift.lesson: In a merger the biggest risk is people leaving with their knowledge. What helps is knowledge sharing across companies and retrospectives where people from both cultures agree on a shared way of working – not one side's rules imposed on the other.

gate.title: Joint steering committee
gate.text: The steering committee, with people from both the bank and the fintech, decides on the second half of the project. How do you prepare the materials?
gate.lesson: One project needs one picture of its state: milestones of the predictively managed parts and working increments of the agile parts in one overview. Two presentations mean two projects.

choices.text: A joint overview: bank milestones, a live app demo and risks in one place
choices.feedback: For the first time the committee sees one project, not two companies.

choices.text: Two presentations – the bank its Gantt chart, the fintech its demo
choices.feedback: Half the committee only listened to “their” presentation.

choices.text: Report using the bank's template
choices.feedback: The bank is happy. The founder stayed silent at the meeting.

eventSlots.title: What does “done” mean?
eventSlots.text: For the bank a feature is done when security approves it. For the fintech, when it's in the app store. Each side claims the opposite about the “login” feature.
eventSlots.lesson: Merging two cultures needs a shared vocabulary. A Definition of Done is an agreement, not one side's rules taken over.

choices.text: Write a joint Definition of Done: tested, security-reviewed and deployed
choices.feedback: The debate took two hours. Now everyone means the same thing.

choices.text: Let each side do it its own way
choices.feedback: A ceasefire. For now.

choices.text: Adopt the bank's definition
choices.feedback: The fintech sees it as its first defeat.

eventSlots.title: A policy for everything
eventSlots.text: Bank policy says every new app version must go through a forty-page change request.
eventSlots.lesson: Expensive changes (the bank's core) belong in formal change control; cheap ones (the app) can be decided by the Product Owner. Working around rules comes back to bite.

choices.text: Agree on two speeds: core changes via change control, app changes decided by the Product Owner
choices.feedback: Security got what it needs. The fintech can release every week.

choices.text: Comply – every version through the bank's change control board
choices.feedback: The first change request took three people two days.

choices.text: Work around the policy and release quietly
choices.feedback: Fast. And risky.

eventSlots.title: Everything goes through Věra
eventSlots.text: Only Věra understands the core banking system. Every question from the fintech ends up with her and Věra can't keep up.
eventSlots.lesson: A knowledge island is doubly dangerous in a merger: the knowledge sits in one head and in one company. Pairing across companies spreads it.

choices.text: Pair Věra with Tadeáš on the core interface
choices.feedback: Tadeáš asks, Věra explains. After a week he answers half the questions himself.

choices.text: Věra can handle it, she's experienced
choices.feedback: Věra is handling it. For now.

choices.text: Bring in a consultant from the core vendor
choices.feedback: The consultant helped. The knowledge will leave with him.

eventSlots.title: Two cultures in one meeting
eventSlots.text: Bank people talk about “the fintech kids”, the fintech about “the dinosaurs”. Meetings turn into tug-of-war.
eventSlots.lesson: A culture clash isn't solved by separating teams, but by working together. Mixed pairs and joint retrospectives build one team.

choices.text: Mixed pairs on every feature and a joint retrospective
choices.feedback: The first week was bumpy. By the second, people were inviting each other to lunch.

choices.text: Split teams by company so they don't fight
choices.feedback: Peace. Each team does its own thing.

choices.text: Team building at a spa hotel
choices.feedback: It was nice. On Monday the old jokes were back.

eventSlots.title: The founder wants crypto
eventSlots.text: The fintech founder wants crypto in the app. “Without it young customers won't take us seriously.”
eventSlots.lesson: A powerful stakeholder's idea is a hypothesis like any other. A cheap experiment decides better than hierarchy.

choices.text: Test customer interest with a cheap experiment before building anything
choices.feedback: A landing page showed interest from 2 % of customers. The founder took it gracefully.

choices.text: Postpone until after launch
choices.feedback: The founder wrote it in his notebook. In red.

choices.text: Build it now – the founder has a vision
choices.feedback: The bank learned about crypto from the internal chat.

eventSlots.title: The regulator asks questions
eventSlots.text: The regulator wants to know how the project decides on app changes and who is accountable for them.
eventSlots.lesson: Agile doesn't mean undocumented decisions. In a regulated environment it must be clear who decided what – even in the backlog.

choices.text: Present the rules: change control for the core and a log of Product Owner decisions for the app
choices.feedback: The regulator closed its inquiry.

choices.text: Answer that the fintech decides in an agile way and documentation isn't needed
choices.feedback: The regulator requested a full process audit.

choices.text: Write the documentation retroactively
choices.feedback: Milan wrote for three evenings. It passed.

eventSlots.title: Fintech customers are worried
eventSlots.text: Word is spreading on social media that after the merger fintech customers will lose their favorite features.
eventSlots.lesson: Change for people needs transparency and a chance to try new things in advance. Migrating without warning destroys trust.

choices.text: Publish the migration plan and let customers try a beta
choices.feedback: Beta testers write more praise than complaints.

choices.text: Move everyone at once without warning
choices.feedback: Fast. The app rating dropped to 1.9.

choices.text: Send an FAQ email
choices.feedback: 11 % of customers opened it.

eventSlots.title: Milan got an offer
eventSlots.text: Milan, the team's only security specialist, got an offer from a competitor.
eventSlots.lesson: It's good to keep a key person – but above all, make sure their knowledge doesn't leave with them.

choices.text: Counteroffer, and Milan trains a colleague in AML
choices.feedback: Milan stayed and now two people understand security.

choices.text: Let him go, it'll work out somehow
choices.feedback: Milan left on Friday. On Monday the first audit question arrived.

choices.text: Hire an external security firm
choices.feedback: The contractors are good. And expensive.

eventSlots.title: A test crashed the bank's environment
eventSlots.text: A fintech integration test took down the core banking test environment for a day. The bank is furious.
eventSlots.lesson: A bug at the interface of two companies is a chance to learn together. Hunting for a culprit splits the team; banning tests pushes bugs into live operations.

choices.text: A joint blameless root-cause analysis and an updated test procedure
choices.feedback: Cause: a missing call limit. Procedure fixed, nobody lost face.

choices.text: Blame the fintech
choices.feedback: The bank calmed down. The fintech remembered whose side you're on.

choices.text: Ban tests on the bank's environment
choices.feedback: The environment is safe. Bugs will now be found in production.

eventSlots.title: The board wants to launch earlier
eventSlots.text: A competitor announced a similar app. The board wants to launch a month earlier.
eventSlots.lesson: Schedule pressure can be met with a staged launch (an employee pilot), not by overloading the team.

choices.text: Launch early only for employees as a pilot, for customers on schedule
choices.feedback: Employees found 14 bugs before customers did.

choices.text: Promise an earlier launch
choices.feedback: The promise is out. The team learned about it from the press release.

choices.text: Refuse, pointing to the plan
choices.feedback: The board accepted it. Without enthusiasm.

eventSlots.title: The night before launch
eventSlots.text: Everything is ready. How do you release the app to customers?
eventSlots.lesson: A staged rollout (a small percentage of customers first) limits the impact of bugs the tests missed.

choices.text: Gradually: 5 % of customers, watch, then more
choices.feedback: On day one a payments bug showed up. It hit only a few hundred customers.

choices.text: Everyone at once at midnight
choices.feedback: In the morning payments didn't work. For anyone.

choices.text: Postpone a week to be safe
choices.feedback: An extra week of testing. The founder is furious.

nehotovo.title: A “done” feature failed the audit
nehotovo.text: A feature the fintech reported as done failed the bank's security review.
nehotovo.lesson: Without a shared definition of done, hidden unfinished work piles up. Sooner or later someone finds it – worst case, a customer.
nehotovo.unresolvedText: After launch it turned out some “done” features never passed the security review.

choices.text: Introduce a joint Definition of Done now and finish the feature
choices.feedback: Late, but better than never.

choices.text: Launch it anyway
choices.feedback: Bank security made a note of it.

choices.text: Turn the feature off
choices.feedback: Safe. Customers lost the feature.

audit_nalez.title: Internal audit found secret releases
audit_nalez.text: The bank's internal audit found that the fintech shipped three app versions outside the approved process.
audit_nalez.lesson: Working around rules solves speed only in the short term. The sustainable fix is to change the rules to match the risk of each change.
audit_nalez.unresolvedText: A year later the audit found unreported app versions and the bank was fined.

choices.text: Admit it and agree on rules based on change risk
choices.feedback: Audit closed with a recommendation. The rules are more sensible.

choices.text: Sweep it under the rug
choices.feedback: The auditor wasn't having it.

choices.text: Freeze releases for a month
choices.feedback: Safe. Customers noticed nothing is happening.

rozhrani.title: Two teams, two interfaces
rozhrani.text: The bank team and the fintech team each built their own version of the interface between the app and the core. They don't fit.
rozhrani.lesson: Separate teams in one project create separate solutions. An interface needs a joint team and integration tests.
rozhrani.unresolvedText: The interface between the app and the core breaks with every new version.

choices.text: A mixed team for the interface and joint integration tests
choices.feedback: One interface, one team.

choices.text: Let each team fix its own part
choices.feedback: Now they don't fit in a different way.

choices.text: Hire an integrator
choices.feedback: The integrator glued it together.
